# ADR-0028 — S1.4 contract clarifications (deleted-slot rule, report preconditions, comment-count trigger vs `profiles_guard`, schema helper names, `commentBodySchema` home, banned reach, moderator merge read)

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-09-03

## Slice
S1.4

## Context
Kind: deviation
- Spec says: `docs/build/00-build-plan.md` §S1.4.AC8 — "deleted comment with replies shows 'Deleted.' slot with replies intact; without replies the slot still stays (per §11.2)"; `docs/build/05-test-plan.md` T-E2E-3 — anon on seed sees "**3 TOTAL**" (`…0205` "'Deleted.' slot only if it has replies (none on seed)"); `docs/build/03-components.md` §2.2 `SectionTitle` — "N TOTAL = published + own held/hidden + 'Deleted.'/'Hidden by a moderator.' slots"; `DESIGN.md` §11.2 — "**Deleted with replies:** the slot stays as 'Deleted.'". `docs/build/04-server-contracts.md` §1.2 `reportComment` Preconditions — "Comment `status='published'`"; §5.1 M8 — "(held/hidden/deleted comment) … reports accepted (unique) but no status change"; 05 T-ACT-22 — "M8: report on hidden `…0204` by a mod → accepted". `docs/data-model.md` §2.1 — `comment_count` "maintained by trigger"; migration `20260821090000_profiles_guard_reserved_and_banned.sql` (ADR-0020) — `profiles_guard()` raises 42501 when a JWT caller changes `comment_count`. `docs/build/_registry.md` Modules — `validation/comment.ts` = "`commentBodySchema`, `stripHtml`, `countLinks`, `linkify`, `commentErrorLine`"; ADR-0008 D3 / ADR-0013 addendum — zod stays out of client-reachable modules (the S1.1 `handleSchema` precedent lives in `lib/actions/accounts.schema.ts`). 03 §2.4 `ModActionRow` props — `{ commentId, authorId, authorHandle, status, onDone? }`.
- Found: (1) 00 AC8's parenthetical contradicts 05 T-E2E-3's seed count, 03 §2.2 and DESIGN §11.2 (all three keep a "Deleted." slot only while it has visible replies); a deleted reply has no children by construction (one level). (2) 04 §1.2's `reportComment` precondition row contradicts its own §5.1 M8 and 05 T-ACT-22, which are the executable contract. (3) The `comment_count` maintenance trigger runs inside the JWT session that inserted/approved the comment; `profiles_guard()` sees `auth.role() = 'authenticated'` and refuses the `comment_count` change (and, for a banned author being approved, any own-row write) — the S1.1 guard and the S1.4 trigger cannot both hold as written; the same applies to `comments.like_count` under the new `comments_guard()`. (4) data-model §2.11 names `can_comment`, `comments_set_status()` and `moderator_thread` but the build also needs the visibility predicate in one place (policies, `can_comment`, the view, the RPC) and the two counter triggers and an UPDATE guard, none of which the registry names. (5) `lib/validation/comment.ts` is imported by the comment client islands (`linkify`, `commentErrorLine`), so a zod schema there would ship zod to the browser — the exact ADR-0008 D3 case. (6) `/admin/comments` needs Unhide · Delete · Rename handle on the same row as Approve · Hide · Ban (02 §1.3, 00 AC14); 03 §2.4 lists the row's props for the thread only. (7) 03 §2.4 `CommentThread` and 00 §S1.4 Scope-IN say the optimistic insert is skipped only for *first-timers* under `hold_first_time`, but the client cannot tell a first-timer apart: 03 C-17a exposes `id, handle, avatar_path, role, is_banned` and never `comment_count`. (8) 01 INV-66, the 01 folder list and "Module ownership" prose, and 05 T-UNIT-4 still place `commentBodySchema` in `lib/validation/comment.ts` after Decision 5 moved it; 04 §1.2 `postComment` Effects and data-model §2.5 carry the first-timer qualifier of (7) (found by `spec-drift-reviewer`, Session B rounds 1–2).
- Related: `docs/questions.md` S1.4 build notes 2026-09-03 · ADR-0020 (guard) · ADR-0027 (the S1.3 clarifications precedent).

## Decision
1. **Deleted slot rule.** A `deleted` root comment renders (and counts) as a "Deleted." slot only while it has at least one visible reply; a deleted root without visible replies and a deleted reply disappear from the thread. 00 S1.4.AC8 is amended to that wording; 05 T-E2E-3 (3 TOTAL on seed), 03 §2.2 and DESIGN §11.2 stand as written.
2. **`reportComment` preconditions.** A report is accepted on any existing, non-deleted comment whose target is visible (`can_comment` binds the RLS insert); auto-hold applies only to a `published` comment by a non-moderator author (04 §5.1 M6/M7); held/hidden comments accept the report with no status change (M8). The 04 §1.2 precondition row is amended; §5.1 and T-ACT-22 are unchanged.
3. **Counter triggers vs guards.** `profiles_guard()` and the new `comments_guard()` skip their JWT-caller column rules when `pg_trigger_depth() > 1` — a write issued by another trigger (`comments_bump_comment_count()` on `profiles.comment_count`, `comment_likes_count()` on `comments.like_count`) is a system write, never a browser PATCH (a PATCH runs at depth 1; users cannot create triggers). Migration `20260903090400_profiles_guard_nested_triggers.sql` re-issues `profiles_guard()` with only that change (ADR-0020's rules are otherwise verbatim).
4. **Schema names (registry add-first).** Helper `comment_target_visible(text, uuid)` (security definer; project → `project_is_visible`, every other target type → false in v1 — ADR-0002 C21) is the one visibility predicate used by the `comments` SELECT policy, `can_comment`, `comments_public` and `moderator_thread`. Trigger functions: `comments_guard()` (BEFORE UPDATE on `comments` — the 05 T-RLS-71..77 column rules: body edits by the author within 15 min only; `like_count`/`author_id`/`target_*`/`parent_id`/`created_at` immutable for JWT callers; an author may set `deleted` only; a moderator may set any status and gets `moderated_by/at` stamped when acting on someone else's row), `comments_bump_comment_count()` (AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF status; +1 the first time a row reaches `published`, never −1), `comment_likes_count()` (AFTER INSERT/DELETE on `comment_likes`). `comments_public` exposes exactly `id, target_type, target_id, parent_id, status, created_at, like_count, body, author_id, edited_at` (05 T-RLS-128's set); `comments.author_id` is nullable with `on delete set null` so a deleted account's comments survive as "Deleted." slots (04 §1.1 `deleteAccount`, 05 T-ACT-65).
5. **`commentBodySchema` home.** The zod schema lives in `lib/actions/comments.schema.ts` (with `postCommentInput` etc.) and refines on the pure `validateBody()` in `lib/validation/comment.ts`, which stays zod-free — the `handleSchema` precedent (ADR-0008 D3, ADR-0013). 04 §1.2 B-rules and the registry Modules line are amended; 05 T-UNIT-4 imports the schema from the schema file.
6. **`ModActionRow` admin surface.** `ModActionRow` gains the additive prop `surface?: 'thread' | 'admin'` (default `'thread'`; C-03 additive-prop precedent — ADR-0014, ADR-0027 D6). Under `surface="admin"` the row also renders Unhide (hidden rows), Delete (`InlineConfirm` danger) and Rename handle (`Field` + `InlineConfirm tone="neutral"` → `renameUserHandle`) — the composition 03 §2.4 already describes for the queue row — and refreshes the dynamic page after each action.
7. **Moderator reads (the recorded 02-vs-05 tension).** `/admin/comments` and the sidebar/dashboard held count read only `comments`, `comment_reports`, `public_profiles` and `projects_public`, all of which the frozen T-RLS matrix grants to moderators — no RLS change and no widening is needed for S1.4; the tension logged for hidden projects / `sync_runs` (S1.2 notes) stays open and unchanged.

8. **Banned viewers never reach a thread.** The proxy (02 §3 M4b, ADR-0019) sends a banned account to `/banned` before any page renders, so `CommentThread`'s `banned` shell ("You can't comment here." + dim `Avatar`) is reachable only when a session is banned mid-page (the `ViewerProvider` re-read). 05 T-E2E-28 and the "that user sees the banned state" clause of T-E2E-30 assert the observable outcome — `/projects/<slug>` → 307 `/banned`, no composer anywhere — and 00 S1.4.AC10's composer clause is read the same way; the shell stays as built (03 §2.4) for the mid-session case.
9. **Moderator merge reads `public_profiles`.** RPC `moderator_thread` returns `author_id` only, so `CommentThread`, for moderators, resolves the authors the RPC introduced through the public view `public_profiles` on the same browser client (ids from the RPC result only). 03 C-17 exception 5 and 02 §2.3 "one further read, moderators only" gain that read; it is the 01 INV-45 cross-user read, never `profiles`. `CommentView` gains the moderators-only optional `reportCount?: number` (the RPC's `report_count`, the counterpart of `isFirstComment`) — 04 §1.2 and 03 §2.4 type lines amended.
10. **`renameUserHandleInput.handle` is a plain string** (≤ 64 chars): the H1/H3 verdict and its code (`validation` / `handle_reserved` / `handle_taken`) come from RPC `check_handle` as 04 §1.2 Preconditions and 05 T-ACT-67 require — a zod-level `handleSchema` would answer `validation` for a reserved name and make `handle_reserved` unreachable (the `completeOnboarding` precedent). The RPC runs under the moderator's own session (04 §1.2 says "evaluated as the target" — there is no way to run it as another user): its "taken" test excludes the moderator's row, so a rename onto the moderator's own handle is answered by the unique index (`handle_taken` all the same), and a case-only rename of the target's current handle answers `handle_taken` — accepted.
11. **`stripHtml` drops `<script>…</script>` blocks whole** before the 04 B1 tag regex runs (05 T-UNIT-5: `<script>alert(1)</script>x` → `x`); the B1 regex is otherwise verbatim, so every other tag still becomes nothing and its text stays.
12. **The direct write path binds the action rules (the ADR-0020 lesson).** For a JWT caller the DB itself enforces what the actions enforce: `comments_set_status()` pins `created_at`/`updated_at` to `now()` (a forged stamp would open an edit window that never closes) and refuses a `parent_id` that is not a published root on the same target; `comments_guard()` refuses an `edited_at` that moves without a body edit or precedes `created_at` (the stamp itself stays the action's — 04 §1.2 "no trigger" — so a direct body PATCH inside the window is the one unflagged write the letter allows; T-RLS-71 asserts that PATCH); the three tables carry column-level INSERT grants (`comments`: `id, target_type, target_id, author_id, parent_id, body, status` · `comment_likes`: `comment_id, user_id` · `comment_reports`: `id, comment_id, reporter_id, reason, note`; `comment_reports` UPDATE is `resolved_at, resolved_by` only) so counters, moderation columns and timestamps are never client-writable; and `comments_set_status()` keeps a backstop on direct inserts — 60 comments / minute and 600 / day per author, twelve times the 04 §5.5 ceilings — that a script bypassing `postComment` (and its `rate_limit_hits` limiter, ADR-0002 A4) still meets. The action layer is unchanged; every user-facing limit and code stays where 04 puts it.
13. **Optimistic insert only under `auto`.** `CommentThread` performs the optimistic insert only when `moderationMode = 'auto'`; under `hold_first_time` nobody gets one — the bubble appears on the action's return with the status as stored (`held` → `HeldNotice`, `published` → normal), so a held comment never flashes as published (ADR-0002 #72's goal) and the client needs no `comment_count`. 03 §2.4 `CommentThread` and 00 §S1.4 Scope-IN / Risks are amended to that wording; 03 C-17a stays as written. (Session-B spec-drift finding; the code already read it this way.)

## Alternatives considered
| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| Keep every deleted comment as a slot (00 AC8 letter) | Breaks 05 T-E2E-3's binding count, contradicts DESIGN §11.2 and 03 §2.2; empty "Deleted." slots for reply-less roots are noise. |
| Reject reports on non-published comments (04 §1.2 letter) | Contradicts §5.1 M8 and T-ACT-22; moderators legitimately report held/hidden rows they can see. |
| Bump `comment_count` from the action via the service client instead of a trigger | Data-model §2.1 and 05 T-RLS-126 require the trigger (a direct JWT insert must count too). |
| Use a session setting (`set_config`) to let the guards through | A flag any SQL in the session could set; `pg_trigger_depth()` cannot be forged from PostgREST. |
| Inline the visibility `case` in each of the four SQL sites | Four copies of the v1 target rule to keep in step; one definer helper is the ADR-0022 pattern. |
| Put `commentBodySchema` in `lib/validation/comment.ts` (registry letter) | Ships zod into the comment islands (ADR-0008 D3); the S1.1 `handleSchema` precedent already settled the pattern. |
| A separate `AdminCommentActions` component | A second component with the same three buttons; 03 C-22 reuse rule prefers the additive prop. |
| Exempt `/projects/*` from the banned redirect so the banned shell renders | A product change to ADR-0019 (David's decision: a banned account sees `/banned` and nothing else); the shell costs nothing and covers the mid-session case. |
| Widen `moderator_thread` to return handle/avatar | Duplicates `public_profiles` inside a definer RPC; the public view is the sanctioned cross-user read (01 INV-45). |
| Trust the actions alone for reply shape, timestamps and limits | The S1.1 round-3 finding (questions.md 2026-08-21): the browser holds the anon key + its own JWT and can write the tables directly; every action rule needs its DB twin. |
| Keep `handleSchema` on `renameUserHandleInput` | A reserved name would fail zod first and answer `validation`, hiding `handle_reserved` (04 §1.2 / T-ACT-67). |
| Expose `comment_count` through C-17a so the client can spot first-timers | Widens the viewer shape (01 INV-45 territory) for a cosmetic optimisation; a non-first-timer under hold mode waits one round-trip instead. |

## Consequences
- Positive: one executable reading of the deleted/report/counter rules; the guards stay strict for browsers while the system triggers work; the schema has one visibility predicate.
- Negative: `profiles_guard()` is re-issued (third version); the registry gains three trigger-function names and one helper; 03 §2.4 `ModActionRow` grows a prop.
- Follow-ups: S1.7 wires `comment_target_visible` for `skin`/`art` when those threads open (Phase 2 — ADR-0002 C21) → owner `supabase-ops`.
